Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rongon Mukhopadhyay Hon'Ble Mr. Justice
Pradeep Kumar Srivastava For the Appellant : Mr. Ashok Kumar, Advocate For the State :
APP ---
Order No. 04 Dated 02nd December, 2025 I.A. No. 13477 of 2025 Heard the learned counsel for the respective parties.
This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.

The appellant has been convicted for the offences u/s 376(1) and 307 of the IPC and has been sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life along with a fine of Rs. 4,00,000/- for the offence u/s 376(1) IPC.
It has been alleged that the marriage of the appellant and the victim was fixed, but the marriage was kept on hold but the appellant was regularly conversing with the sister of the victim.
The appellant had refused to solemnize marriage and instead continued conversing with the sister of the informant.

It has been alleged that on 18.04.2022, the appellant had called the sister of the informant and gave her a Sari in gift and when the sister of the informant returned home, she was found drenched in blood.
It has further been alleged that the neck of the sister of the informant was slit.

Submission has been advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant that the evidence of the Doctor who has been examined as PW-9 clearly reveals that no injury was found on the person of the deceased.
It has further been submitted that the age of the victim was assessed to be between 22-23 years and no evidence of recent sexual intercourse was also detected.
Learned counsel adds that the appellant is in custody since 06.05.2022.

sentences.text: Learned A.P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.

Regard being had to the evidence of the victim who has been examined as PW-6 and the fact that no injury was found on the person of the victim as per PW-9 apart from the period of custody undergone by the appellant, we are inclined to admit the appellant on bail.

Accordingly, during pendency of this appeal, the appellant is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rs. Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned trial court [Additional Sessions Judge-II,
Latehar] in connection with S. T. No. 264 of 2022.
This I.A. stands allowed and disposed of.
(RONGON MUKHOPADHYAY, J.) (PRADEEP KUMAR SRIVASTAVA, J.) 02.12.2025 MK Uploaded on 4.12.2025 Page|2
